title: MNQ momentum system Backtest Result
author: FossilBlade
selftext:
I'll be as open about this as I can. The one thing I keep is the entry trigger.  
  
**What it is**  
  
A momentum system on MNQ, 5-minute bars, fully automated on NinjaTrader. It has no opinion about direction. When price does something decisive, it goes with it.  
  
**How it runs**  
  
\- Signals are read at the close of each 5-minute bar, and the entry goes in at market right after.  
\- One contract, one position at a time. No adding, no averaging down, no martingale, no grid.  
\- Every trade gets a hard stop the moment it fills, the same distance every time.  
\- Once a trade is up by that same distance, the stop starts trailing tight behind the best price. There's no profit target.  
\- A decisive move the other way closes the trade and reverses it.  
\- It trades the overnight session too. It goes flat at 16:45 New York and takes nothing new until the 18:00 reopen.  
  
Over the last year 45% of trades ended on the trailing stop, 37% on the stop loss, 15% were reversed by an opposite signal and 2% closed at the daily flatten.  
  
**The numbers**  
  
TradingView backtest, the last 12 months to 20 Oct 2026, 1 MNQ, $0.50 a side commission.  
  
\- 4,907 trades, about 19 a day. 49% winners; the average winner was $80 and the average loser $69.  
\- Net +$20,362.  
\- Max drawdown $2,120. The longest stretch without a new high was 51 days, mid-April to early June.  
\- Worst day −$703, best day +$1,018. The longest losing run was 5 days in a row.  
  
  
| Month | P&L |  
|---|---|  
| Oct 2025 (from the 20th) | −$86 |

What I'm not sharing is the entry trigger and the exact settings. Ask me about anything else.

comments.author: wkerstens
comments.body:
Quite some trades per day. How did you account for costs and slippage? It does look pretty solid though.  
The issue is usually have with trailing stops is that they get caught in the noise, killing the trends.

Do you plan on taking it live?

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Good question, and it's the main one for me too. At 19 trades a day, the commission is only part of it, since the backtest probably fills at the signal price while a live market order will give up a tick or two each time. I'd also keep an eye on the trailing stop point, because the 45% of trades that ended on it are the ones to check against a wider or noisier setting.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Thanks for sharing this much, and the monthly table and trade-exit split are more than most people post. A few questions I'd ask: how many parameters were tuned on this same 12 months, since the settings are private? And does it still hold on data before Oct 2025? With 19 trades a day, a small change in slippage matters a lot, so I'd rerun it with 1 or 2 ticks of slippage per side. Average winner $80 against average loser $69 leaves a thin margin. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is one place to run a test like that with fees and slippage.
